verdict.reason: Verified independently. `editor.ts:3598` (`indent()`) and `:3624` (`outdent()`) enter `doc.batch(() => { docStore.snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...) })` with no `recordCursorForHistory()` call, while the three keyboard equivalents in `text-editor.ts:2719`, `:2782`, `:2801` each call it explicitly before the batch with a comment stating it must be outside. The store confirms the consequence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:2924-2927`), `setCursorForHistory` (`:3054-3060`) is the only staging point for `pendingCursorPos`, `consumePendingCursor()` (`:3143`) returns null when it was never called, and every write path only records history presence `if (cursorForHistory)` (e.g. `:2720-2724`). `skipNonHistoryPresence()` (`:3210-3212`), keyed on the `activeRoot` set by `batch()` (`:2902-2911`), independently confirms the flush cannot be issued from inside the batch. Both toolbar entry points are reachable from `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949,953` and `text-paragraph-group.tsx:212,230` with no intervening adapter that stages the cursor. This is a reachable second entry point that bypasses an ordering invariant the change establishes elsewhere, leaving undo's caret/selection restoration wrong on that path — in-lane and blocking at major.

mergedFrom.summary: The two copies of `siblingsOf` disagree on how a stale parent map is tolerated: text-editor's throws where editor.ts's degrades
`TextEditor.siblingsOf` resolves the parent table with throwing `getBlock`, where its `editor.ts` twin deliberately uses non-throwing `findBlock` for the same stale-map reason

finding.summary: New crash path: TextEditor.siblingsOf resolves the parent table with doc.getBlock (throws), unlike the editor.ts twin which deliberately uses findBlock
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2890 `const tableBlock = this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId);` — `getCellInfo` reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, which is only as fresh as the last layout pass. This file already treats that map as routinely stale: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2971-2978 wraps arrow handling in try/catch with the comment "Stale blockParentMap data (e.g. table rows removed by remote edit)", and `Doc.getBlock` throws when the id no longer resolves (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:220-266 / findBlock returning undefined). `handleTab` (2699-2707), `handleIndent` (2762) and `handleOutdent` (2779) have no such guard, and before this change the cursor-only path never consulted the parent map at all — so a Tab/Cmd+] with the caret in a cell of a table deleted by a peer now throws out of the keydown handler mid-gesture. The diff's own editor.ts copy documents the opposite choice (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1632-1641, `findBlock`, "rather than throw out of the middle of an indent gesture"); the fix belongs on the new text-editor.ts code (use findBlock + optional chaining).

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. `TextEditor.siblingsOf` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2920-2922) is `return this.doc.siblingBlocksOf(block.id) ?? [block];` — it contains no parent-map lookup and no `doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)` call. The quoted evidence line, text-editor.ts:2890, is actually `fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks);` inside the top-level multi-block table walk. The `editor.ts` "twin" the finding contrasts it with (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1635-1636) is the identical one-liner `doc.siblingBlocksOf(block.id) ?? [block];`, so the claimed divergence between the two files does not exist either. `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:311-328) resolves the parent table with the non-throwing `findBlock` (line 320, defined 245-255) plus optional chaining, and falls back to `walkCellsForSiblings`, returning `undefined` instead of throwing — precisely the behaviour the finding says is missing. A repo-wide grep for `info.tableBlockId` finds it only at text-editor.ts:3800/3803 and table-layout.ts:386, none on the Tab/indent/outdent path. Therefore no new `getBlock`-throws crash path is introduced on the cursor-only Tab/Cmd+] path.

finding.summary: The new `levelOf` normalization protects only the planner; the layout pass still reads `listLevel` raw, where a non-finite value throws a RangeError and takes the whole layout down
finding.evidence: `list-level.ts` normalizes at "the single point of read" and its own comment concedes the layout "reads `listLevel` raw" — but the unprotected reader is worse than bad geometry. `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1091` does `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` with `const level = block.listLevel ?? 0` (line 1089). With `level = NaN` that assignment is `arr.length = NaN` → `RangeError: Invalid array length` out of `computeLayout`; with a large finite level (> 2^32-1) the same. `layout.ts:494` also multiplies it into the indent. The value is reachable unvalidated: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` does `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` on a peer's Tree attribute, and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` serializes whatever the content ingest supplies (`String(block.listLevel)`, no clamp, no schema bound anywhere in packages/backend/src). The diff's claim that a poisoned level is "repaired by the gesture that touches it" cannot hold here: layout runs on first render, before any gesture. Fix belongs on the raw readers (reuse the new `levelOf`/`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` in `layout.ts`), not on the planner.

verdict.reason: The finding claims layout.ts reads `listLevel` raw at both the indent multiplication and the `levelCounters.length` assignment. Both cited sites already call the new normalizer. `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1097` reads `const level = normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel);` immediately before `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` at line 1099, with a comment (1092-1096) naming the exact RangeError/large-allocation hazard the finding describes; `layout.ts:497` reads `LIST_INDENT_PX * (normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel) + 1)`, and the import is at `layout.ts:17`. Since `normalizeListLevel` (model/list-level.ts:42-46) returns 0 for non-finite input and clamps to [0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL=8], neither NaN nor a large finite level can reach either expression. The ingest path quoted as unvalidated is also clamped: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:501` is `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))` (import at line 50), not the bare `Number(...)` the finding quotes, and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:250` applies the same clamp at the engine's Tree→Block boundary. The other raw readers the finding's rationale invokes are guarded too (serialize/markdown.ts:145, export/pdf-painter.ts:370 and 593). The reviewer's cited line numbers (494, 1089-1091) are pre-guard offsets; the guards plus their comments shifted the code, which explains the empty grep of those ranges.
